item.title: Ask The Person Above You A Question (PART IX): Re: @Truc Linh
item.content:encoded:
What was the last book you read?

I can’t recall the last book I finished, but I’m currently reading The 7 Habits of Highly Effective Teens for English class.

Would you recommend it?

That’s a tough one. I personally feel like the book itself will not appeal to everyone (I know that’s every book, but this one really hits that mark), especially since it was written specifically for teens. I personally did not connect or relate to most of most stories and experiences from within it so far. Honestly, after reading most of it, I haven’t really retained much info. Most of the time, I felt like most of the context in the book was stuff I already knew that made me go “yeah, yeah, yeah, I get the point”. There were also some parts where the phrasing was unnecessarily condescending, which contradicts what most of what the book is trying to communicate. I know nothing is perfect, but I feel like some of the phrases could’ve been rephrased better. Adding onto the condescension, I also feel like the book doesn’t really acknowledge certain viewpoints and certain situations when stating its personal opinions. The book also felt a little too overly positive, and I was really hoping to see a little more deeper stuff and how to pull through certain tough situations using the advice provided. (Maybe once I finish it.)

I admit, though, it provides really good advice and eye opening viewpoints. However, I haven’t really tried out any of the book's activities yet due to other obligations, so I haven’t really gotten the chance to fully experience what the book has to offer. For me, if I had the time to try out the activities, I’d probably feel less inclined to just read it and forget about it. Overall, the book has really good information to consider. I do feel like the book could’ve been better; I can probably write a whole essay of nit-picks on it. As for recommendation, I’d probably recommend it to those who might be interested in changing their lifestyle or just want some good quotes to look at. This is just my opinion though, and obviously the book doesn’t really appeal much to me. Honestly, if someone is interested in reading something, they should just go for it.
